newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - Jan 3.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - Jan 3.

text.p: The New York Times reported the following business stories on Friday:
- Some large retail chains reported disappointing sales on Thursday for the end of last year.
- In a milestone on the road to deregulated telephone service, the Ameritech Corp applied for permission to offer long distance service within its own region.

- The nation's nuclear power plants are delivering record quantities of electricity, but there are fears that many plants will become financial albatrosses as deregulation gives business and residential customers choices about where they buy power.
- Before a late rebound, the stock market almost opened 1997 the way it ended 1996 - with a big drop.
- Bank of New York said it would raise its stake to 9.9 percent in State Street Boston.
- Philip Duff, Morgan Stanley's chief financial officer, has been tapped to be chief executive and president of Van Kampen American Capital, a mutual fund company Morgan Stanley acquired last year.
- A report that manufacturing picked up strength in December sent bond prices down.
- De Beers Consolidated Mines of South Africa confirmed it would end a marketing agreement with Russia, citing Russian politics and bureaucracy.
- In a new advertising campaign for computer printers, Hewlett-Packard gently pokes fun at its own engineers in an effort to make its technology seem more accessible.
